items.headline: Strait of Hormuz tanker attacks hit wartime high; Brent holds near $106
items.summary: Iran's IRGC has sharply escalated tanker strikes in the Strait of Hormuz this week -- the highest pace since the Iran war began in Feb 2026 -- with a Houthi missile reportedly striking an Aramco facility near Dhahran and a container ship confirmed hit near the strait. Brent traded near $105.66-107, WTI near $96-98.
items.actionable: Sustained Hormuz risk premium supports the safe-haven bid underpinning the book's gold/silver miner longs even as it raises tail risk for broad equity exposure.

items.headline: Fed Chair Warsh speaks in Bangkok today (11:30 SGT) -- first public remarks since hot CPI
items.summary: Warsh holds a fireside chat with IMF's Georgieva at the IMF/World Bank annual meetings -- his first public appearance since Wednesday's hot CPI reignited October rate-hike bets. No set policy agenda, but markets are watching for any hint on whether an Oct 27-28 hike is 'live'.
items.actionable: Watch Warsh's tone live -- a hawkish signal pressures the book's SGX bank/REIT holdings further, while a dovish/neutral framing would extend Thursday's precious-metals relief rally.

items.headline: BOE Governor Bailey speaks in Bangkok today (10:00 SGT)
items.summary: Bailey gives a fireside chat at the IIF annual meeting in Bangkok. Markets have priced in a near-certain November BOE hike after a split 6-3 September hold at 3.75% amid energy-driven inflation above target.
items.actionable: Low direct portfolio impact, but a hawkish Bailey reinforces the 'global central banks still fighting inflation' narrative that has been driving both the bond selloff and the gold bid -- a cross-check ahead of Warsh's remarks later today.

items.headline: Thursday's US data: PPI and retail sales ran hot, Philly Fed cooled sharply -- yet stocks reversed higher
items.summary: September core PPI rose at its fastest monthly pace in five months and retail sales grew 0.8% vs 0.4% expected, both inflationary prints; Philly Fed manufacturing dropped to 20.9 from 37.8. Despite the hot data, bond yields reversed lower intraday (10Y to ~5.08-5.09% from ~5.3%) and the dollar weakened, helping drive the S&P +0.33%/Dow +1.08% reversal and the gold/silver rally.
items.actionable: The hot PPI/retail-sales combo keeps a second October Fed hike in play, but Thursday showed yields and the dollar can still fall even on hot data if equity-market stress dominates flows -- a dynamic directly supportive of the book's silver/gold miner sleeve.

items.headline: Global AI/chip-stock rout deepens before partial reversal -- $1tn+ wiped out, Kospi -7.6%, SMIC -3.96%
items.summary: A six-session, ~$1.6-2tn semiconductor selloff accelerated Thursday on AI-capex-financing doubts colliding with rate fears, hitting Korea (Kospi, Samsung -9.5%, SK Hynix -11%), Japan (Nikkei) and Taiwan hardest overnight; Hong Kong's SMIC fell 3.96-4.24% in sympathy. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's public defense of CoreWeave's balance sheet helped stem the rout by Thursday's close.
items.actionable: A global AI-financing scare, not an SMIC-specific issue, directly explains SMIC's weakness -- caution warranted on any near-term bounce until the broader AI-capex de-rating stabilizes.

items.headline: Singapore bank selloff: DBS/OCBC/UOB hit as US 10-yr yield spiked to 5.32%
items.summary: DBS fell ~6%, OCBC ~10%, UOB ~8% between Oct 6-8 as the US 10-year Treasury yield jumped to 5.32% (highest since late 2023), triggering a global bank-stock selloff and profit-taking after a strong 2026 run; the STI fell 3.5% on Oct 8, its biggest single-day drop since April 2025.
items.actionable: The yield-driven de-rating directly pressures the book's bank exposure and is the likely common thread behind Ho Bee Land and other SGX property names' weakness into mid-October -- a sector/yield story, not idiosyncratic.

items.headline: China formalizes rare-earth export control as permanent industrial policy; EU gets only discretionary access
items.summary: China's Central Committee/State Council issued joint guidelines codifying rare-earth export control as a deliberate, permanent lever. EU Trade Commissioner Sefcovic secured only continued processing of existing license applications -- not structural change -- with a key control-wave expiry of Nov 10, 2026 to watch.
items.actionable: China's Nov 10, 2026 control-wave expiry is the next hard catalyst date for the rare-earth watchlist -- a renewal/tightening would be bullish for MP/Lynas re-rating, a quiet lapse would remove near-term urgency from the Western-supply-chain trade.

items.headline: Gold snaps losing streak, silver +2.3% as bond-yield/dollar reversal drives sharp precious-metals rebound
items.summary: December gold rose +$62.20 (+1.51%) to $4,170.10/oz and December silver gained +$1.28 (+2.29%) to $57.16/oz as Treasury yields eased and the dollar weakened amid the tech-stock selloff pushing flows into safe havens -- confirming the backdrop behind SLV/GDX/SILJ/AG's sharp Thursday rallies.
items.actionable: The reversal was driven by falling yields/dollar amid equity stress rather than a dovish Fed pivot -- the miner rally's durability now hinges on today's Warsh/Bailey remarks and whether the chip-stock rout continues to push safe-haven flows into gold/silver.

items.headline: Ho Bee Land -7.50% and Seatrium -4.64% -- no company-specific catalyst found, likely sector/macro spillover
items.summary: Ho Bee Land closed S$1.85 (-7.5%) and Seatrium closed S$1.85 (-4.64%) as the STI fell 0.56%. No SGX filing, profit warning or disclosure explains either move; the best-supported read is cross-currents from the Oct 6-9 bond-yield spike (which also hit DBS/OCBC/UOB) for Ho Bee, and crude softness/broad risk-off for Seatrium (an oil & gas capex-linked name). Ho Bee was mid-buyback (started Oct 7); Seatrium had just renewed its 15-year Carnival maintenance deal and disclosed a $200m buyback -- both inconsistent with a fundamentals-driven selloff.
items.actionable: Flag both for a company-announcement check at SGX open today -- absent a filing, these read as yield/oil-driven sector moves rather than idiosyncratic risk, and the Seatrium buyback/contract newsflow argues against a fundamental deterioration story.

items.headline: Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs post ~$390M net outflows as BTC slides toward $80-81K
items.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs saw a net outflow of 3,209 BTC (7-day: 5,250 BTC) and Ethereum ETFs saw 38,915 ETH outflow (7-day: 133,537 ETH) on Oct 15, totaling ~$390.9M combined, as BTC traded near $80,915 and ETH near $2,360 in sympathy with the broader risk-off from the chip-stock selloff and inflation/rate-hike fears.
items.actionable: Crypto's ETF-outflow-driven weakness is tracking the same risk-off driver as the Asia tech rout -- a useful real-time gauge for whether Friday's Asia open extends Thursday's reversal or resumes the CPI-day selloff, relevant for timing any SGX/HK tech entries from the cash pile.

items.headline: Xiaomi Auto delivers record 40,015 vehicles in September as Sky Nomad SUV ramps
items.summary: Xiaomi's EV unit delivered 40,015 vehicles in September -- its highest monthly total in 2026 -- as the newly launched Sky Nomad extended-range SUV began contributing meaningfully to volumes, though deliveries were still down year-on-year.
items.actionable: Record monthly EV deliveries support the bull case behind Xiaomi's Thursday outperformance (+2.65% even as Tencent/SMIC fell) -- differentiate Xiaomi from the broader HK-tech/chip-sentiment weakness.

items.headline: WTI diverges from Brent -- OPEC+ supply surge offsets Hormuz risk premium
items.summary: WTI fell toward $93 on Oct 14 after OPEC+ reported a sharp September output increase of ~900,000 bpd (to 39.07M bpd average), even as Brent held near $106 on Hormuz/Houthi attack risk and a large 8M-barrel US crude inventory draw for the week ended Oct 9 provided separate support.
items.actionable: The OPEC+ supply surge is a bearish offset to the Hormuz risk premium -- a sustained lower-oil regime would pressure offshore-drilling capex sentiment relevant to the book's Seatrium position even as geopolitical risk keeps headline Brent elevated.

items.headline: Seatrium newsflow (Carnival renewal, Excelerate FSRU contract, buyback) contrasts with Thursday's price drop
items.summary: In the days before Thursday's -4.64% drop, Seatrium renewed its 15-year Carnival Corp cruise-ship maintenance agreement through 2029, signed a full-scope EPCIC FSRU conversion contract with Excelerate Energy, and disclosed a $200m share buyback programme -- none consistent with a fundamentals-driven selloff.
items.actionable: The disconnect between constructive order-book/buyback news and Thursday's price move reinforces that the drop was systemic (yields/oil/risk-off), not company-specific -- supports treating any further SGX-wide dip as a buying opportunity rather than a Seatrium-specific red flag.
